summary: Agents retain access to shell executions from earlier live invocations after claiming work in the same harness incarnation.

replay.detail: Existing native invocation receipts and execution ownership are read directly; nothing is replayed or rebuilt.

schema.detail: No storage, client schema or wire format changes.

rules.detail: Execution ownership and invocation receipts are written as before.

compatibility.detail: Agent execution reads, lists, waits, cancellation and request lookup accept any live invocation of the current incarnation. Immediate acceptance and cancellation transactions check sibling executions and cancellation evidence; cancellation always records every resolved owner key, even when an execution exists. Acknowledged cancellation prevents a paused sibling acceptance, including after tombstone expiry while a cancelled sibling execution remains. Concurrent new live owners outside cancellation's authorization snapshot return retryable resource-request-conflict (HTTP 503); retry the same cancellation to resolve and cancel the new owner's execution. Ended owners are permanently unauthorized (non-retryable resource-exec-owner) and cannot mask a live sibling. Other agents and other incarnations remain isolated. Run credentials retain exact step-attempt scope. Tombstone expiry removes at most 128 rows per operation while preserving seven-day cancellation semantics.
